title: Existence of an ample invertible sheaf descends through a finite cover of a normal integral scheme
statement: Let $f:X\to Z$ be a finite surjective morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Assume that $Z$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and normal, meaning that each local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. If $X$ admits an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then $Z$ admits an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module. No flatness, group action, properness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BD4 (divisors-proposition-push-down-ample), case (2). This is the existence assertion, not descent of a specified sheaf. The proof uses norms after restricting to a dominating integral closed subscheme of X.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], the nonempty irreducible scheme $Z$ has a generic point $\eta$. Surjectivity gives $x\in X$ with $f(x)=\eta$. Put $T=\overline{\{x\}}$, and use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to give $T$ its reduced induced closed subscheme $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$. The closure of one point is irreducible: if $T$ is contained in the union of two closed subsets, the one containing $x$ contains its closure. Thus $Y$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0BD4, proof of case (2): reduction to a dominating reduced integral closed subscheme; Tags 01IS and 01J3 supply the construction.

proof.text: The morphism $p=f\circ i:Y\to Z$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. Its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] and contains $\eta$, so it contains $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Z$; hence $p$ is surjective. Choose an ample invertible module $L$ on $X$. Its restriction $M=i^*L$ is ample on $Y$ by [lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0BD4, proof of case (2); ampleness on the reduced closed subscheme is Tag 01PU.

proof.text: Now $Y,Z$ are integral, $Z$ is normal, and $p$ is finite surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-integral-finite-sheaf-norm] to obtain $d\geq1$ and the restriction-compatible multiplicative maps $\nu_V$ with their scalar-power and vanishing properties. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-norm-invertible-sections] to $p,\nu,M$ and fix the resulting invertible module $N$ on $Z$. Its single choice works for all positive powers and sections.

source.place: Tags 0BD3, 0BCY and 0BCZ, the norm used in the proof of 0BD4(2) via 0BD0.

proof.text: Ampleness of $M$ gives quasi-compactness of $Y$ by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For any open cover of $Z$, its inverse images under $p$ cover $Y$; finitely many cover $Y$. Since $p$ is surjective, those same finitely many opens cover $Z$. Thus $Z$ is quasi-compact.

Fix $z\in Z$ and an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq Z$. The set $E=p^{-1}(\{z\})$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] and is contained in the open $p^{-1}V$. Apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-principal-affine] on $Y$ to $M,E,p^{-1}V$: there are $n>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ with $E\subseteq Y_s\subseteq p^{-1}V$ (and $Y_s$ affine).

source.place: Tag 0BD0, proof: the application of Properties Tag 09NV (lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-norm-invertible-sections] choose $t\in\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n})$ with $Z_t=\{w:p^{-1}(\{w\})\subseteq Y_s\}$. Since $E\subseteq Y_s$, we have $z\in Z_t$. If $w\in Z_t$, surjectivity gives $y\in p^{-1}(\{w\})$; then $y\in Y_s\subseteq p^{-1}V$, so $w\in V$. Consequently $Z_t\subseteq V$, and $Z_t=V\cap Z_t$ is affine by [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open], applied to the invertible module $N$, its positive tensor power $n$, its section $t$ and the affine open $V$.

source.place: Tag 0BD0, final sentences: 0BCZ gives the norm section and Properties Tag 01PV gives affineness.

proof.text: For every $z\in Z$ the preceding construction gives $n\geq1$ and a global section of $N^{\otimes n}$ whose affine nonvanishing open contains $z$. Together with quasi-compactness from step 4, these are exactly the two conditions of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Therefore $N$ is ample, proving the required existence on $Z$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BD4 (proposition-push-down-ample), case (2), using the complete ampleness argument in Tag 0BD0 (lemma-norm-ample).

This is a faithful split of Stacks 0BD4(2), checked at divisors.tex lines 3585-3940. The item statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from live, the base proof was empty, and there is no re-split note. Neither the item nor its citer is on the 2026-10-19 drop list. Steps: 1. 01IS gives the generic point, 01J3 gives the reduced closure of a point over it, and nonempty + reduced + irreducible makes it integral. 2. 035C and 01WK make p finite; the closed image contains η, so p is surjective; 01PU makes i*L ample. 3. The two new norm nodes, with N fixed once before n and s. 4. Quasi-compactness is elementary, by surjectivity. 5. Finite fibre, then 09NV with E = the fibre and W = p^-1 V. 6. The saturated-locus equality gives z in Z_t inside V (shown by choosing a point in each fibre), and 01PV makes Z_t affine. 7. Both clauses of the ample definition hold. New nodes: (a) normal-integral sheaf norm (0BD3 + 0BCX (1),(2)) is true. It is the field norm N_{K/L} with degree [K:L] >= 1; sections embed in K, so it is defined on all opens. Vanishing holds because the constant term b_m lies in fA ∩ B, inside the prime; the source's sign slip does not affect it. (b) The norm-sections node (0BCY/0BCZ) is true. N = Norm(M) with Norm(M^n) = N^n, by the cocycles u^n. For the converse direction of 0BCZ, units go to units after trivializing near the fibre (0BCW), since finite maps are closed. Small cases checked: s = 0, nowhere-vanishing s, the identity map, field extensions. Neither new node is a duplicate: lem-pur-finite-flat-kummer-norm-degree is finite-flat, Noetherian and Kummer; no other node or blueprint node carries 0BD3/0BCY/0BCZ. Neither restates the item. Batch-5 flag on lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion: it is generic Properties 01PU, its 97-node closure contains no other trace-formula or Poincare-duality node, and it is not a step of either assumption, so I accept it.
